extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers studying category theory and related areas (algebra, topology, mathematical logic)
extracted.subtask_description: A textbook-style presentation of core category-theoretic definitions and constructions (categories, functors, 2-categories, bicategories, examples, internal categories in Grp, and axioms for an elementary topos), aimed at explaining formal axioms, coherence conditions, and examples. Useful as a reference for learning or teaching these notions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category (axiomatic presentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A category is a set C of arrows with two functions s, t : C ---> C (source and target) and a partially defined binary operation # (composition), subject to axioms: x # y defined iff s x = t y; s(x#y)=s y; t(x#y)=t x; x#s x = x; t x # x = x; (x # y) # z = x # (y # z) if either side is defined; s s x = s x = t s x; t t x = t x = s t x. An x is an identity iff x = s x (equivalently x = t x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formulation is equivalent to the usual definition in terms of a set of objects and a set of arrows; the axioms list domain/codomain behavior, unit laws, associativity (where defined), and idempotence relations for s and t.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functor (axiomatic formulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A functor F : C ---> D is a function F : C -> D such that sF = F s and tF = F t, and F(x # y) = F x # F y whenever x # y is defined (which implies F x # F y is defined).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This axiomatization is equivalent to the standard object/arrow functor notion; it enforces preservation of source/target and composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2-category as two commuting category structures on one set
rubrics_metrics.description: A 2-category can be viewed as a single set X of 2-cells equipped with two category structures, the 'horizontal' (#0, s0, t0) and the 'vertical' (#1, s1, t1). Each structure satisfies the category axioms, and (i) every identity for the O-structure is an identity for the I-structure; (ii) the two category structures commute with each other (e.g., s0 s1 = s1 s0, s0 t1 = t1 s0, and interchange laws for compositions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commutation means equalities such as s0 s1 = s1 s0, s0 t1 = t1 s0, t0 t1 = t1 t0, and the middle-four interchange: (x #0 y) #1 (u #0 v) = (x #1 u) #0 (y #1 v) when defined. Identities for one structure are identities for the other as specified; the listed equalities (7)-(10) and derived collapsing identities compute composites of s and t and agree with the 2-cell edge picture.

rubrics_metrics.name: n-category / ω-category (multi-level category structures)
rubrics_metrics.description: An n-category is a set X with n different category structures (#_j, s_j, t_j) for j = 0,...,n-1 which commute with each other, and such that an identity for structure i is also an identity for structures j whenever j > i. An ω-category generalizes this to i = 0,1,2,...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put differently, each pair of composition operations #_j and #_i (with j > i) form a 2-category; commuting and identity inclusion conditions extend inductively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bicategory (definition and data)
rubrics_metrics.description: A bicategory B consists of O-cells (objects), I-cells (1-cells), and 2-cells, with for each pair (a,b) an ordinary category B(a,b) whose objects are 1-cells a->b and arrows are 2-cells. Vertical composition of 2-cells is associative with identities. For each triple (a,b,c) there is a bifunctor * : B(b,c) x B(a,b) -> B(a,c) (horizontal composition). For each object a there is an 'identity' 1-cell I_a : a -> a which acts as a unit only up to specified natural isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Horizontal composition * is not strictly associative: associativity holds only up to a specified natural isomorphism α (between two iterated composites). There are likewise natural isomorphisms λ and ρ (the text uses A and p) witnessing left and right unit laws. These natural transformations must satisfy coherence axioms (the pentagon and the triangle) described below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bicategory coherence axioms (pentagon and triangle)
rubrics_metrics.description: The associativity isomorphism α and the unit isomorphisms λ and ρ are subject to two coherence axioms: (1) the pentagon diagram for four composable 1-cells must commute (as in monoidal categories); (2) the left and right identity coherence square/triangle must commute (left and right identities compatibility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the same coherence constraints appearing for monoidal categories; they ensure that all canonical associativity/unit comparisons between iterated composites agree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturality/compatibility condition for 2-cell composites in bicategories
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement that α be a natural transformation amounts to certain commutativity conditions for 2-cells under horizontal and vertical composition (displayed explicitly in the text as commutativity of diagrams like (5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concretely, diagrams equating compositions such as h*(g*I) and (h*g)*I together with the appropriate α and vertical composites must commute; these are the naturality conditions for α and for the unit isomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functor / morphism between bicategories
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a suitable notion of a functor (morphism) between bicategories, which must preserve the bicategory structure up to specified coherent isomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text does not give the detailed definition here but urges the reader to formulate one or consult the literature (Benabou [1967]).

rubrics_metrics.name: Monoidal category as a one-object bicategory
rubrics_metrics.description: Any monoidal category M is a bicategory B with one object: take the objects of M to be the 1-cells of B, the tensor product as horizontal composition, and the arrows of M as 2-cells; the natural isomorphisms (unit and associativity) of M provide the α, λ, ρ required for B. Conversely, a bicategory with one object is a monoidal category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The coherence theorem for monoidal categories gives a coherence result for the maps α, λ, ρ in bicategories as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bicategory of rings, bimodules, and bimodule homomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Define a bicategory where O-cells are rings R,S,T; 1-cells are bimodules B: S <- R (i.e., S-R bimodules); and 2-cells are bimodule homomorphisms. Horizontal composition of 1-cells is given by the tensor product of bimodules B ⊗_S A, which is a T-R bimodule; vertical composition is composition of homomorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associativity of horizontal composition is provided by the standard associativity iso of tensor product, yielding the required associativity isomorphism α. Vertical composition uses the usual composition of module homomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Span bicategory construction (Span(C))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a base category C with all pullbacks, Span(C) is the bicategory with O-cells the objects of C, 1-cells the spans a <- v -> b, and 2-cells maps of span vertices making triangles commute. Horizontal composition of spans is defined by choosing canonical pullbacks of the middle arrows; identities are identity spans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associativity is only up to canonical isomorphism because chosen pullbacks are unique up to iso; the canonical pullback squares and uniqueness up to isomorphism supply the associativity isomorphism and force the pentagon coherence to hold. The identity span and its interactions with composition produce the unit isomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crossed module definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A crossed module is a pair of groups H and P with an action of P on H and a homomorphism α : H -> P respecting the action. If h^p denotes the action of p on h, then for h,k in H and p,q in P the relations include (h k)^p = h^p k^p and α(h^p) = p α(h) p^{-1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crossed modules arise in homotopy theory and are used to relate algebraic and categorical structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal category in Grp determined by diagram and commutator condition
rubrics_metrics.description: An internal category in Grp consists of groups C0 and C1 and group homomorphisms d0,d1,i,μ satisfying the usual internal category conditions. The system is completely determined by the diagram (C1 ->-> C0 via d0,d1 and i) together with the vanishing commutator subgroup [ker d0, ker d1] = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From these data one can reconstruct the categorical composition μ; conversely, a crossed module α: H -> P (with H = ker d0 and P = C0) determines a split exact sequence corresponding to such a diagram. Thus the category of crossed modules is categorically equivalent to the category of such internal category diagrams in Grp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of internal categorical composition by group product
rubrics_metrics.description: In an internal category in Grp the categorical composition μ is determined by the group product in C1 via formulas like μ(g,f) = f ·_{?} g or g ·_{?} f (the text shows equal representations) and middle-four exchange relations ensuring coherence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calculations using identities and the fact that inversion is a functor (in group objects) show the product formulas and symmetry properties, and yield conditions like commutativity of elements from ker d0 and ker d1, explaining the vanishing commutator requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elementary topos axioms (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: An elementary topos is a category with additional structure: a terminal object, pullbacks, truth (a subobject classifier), and power objects. The text presents axioms enumerated as items 6–9 on top of the basic category axioms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These axioms model set-like behavior categorically and yield consequences like all finite products, pullbacks, coproducts, exponentials, and representability of certain hom-sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Axiom 6: Terminal object
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a terminal object 1 such that every object a has exactly one arrow a -> 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Set any singleton set serves; existence of 1 implies products with 1 behave as expected and provides the basis for other constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Axiom 7: Pullbacks
rubrics_metrics.description: Every pair of arrows f: a -> b and g: c -> b with common codomain b has a pullback (fibered product) as in §III.4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In particular taking b = 1 gives binary products a × c. The presence of pullbacks is used in constructions like the span bicategory and in many categorical limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Axiom 8: Truth / subobject classifier
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an object Ω (the object of truth values) and a monomorphism t: 1 -> Ω called truth; to any monomorphism m: a -> b there is a unique arrow χ_m: b -> Ω such that the square with m and χ_m is a pullback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Set take Ω = {0,1} and t the inclusion of 1 to represent characteristic functions; this enables internal characterization of subobjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Axiom 9: Power objects
rubrics_metrics.description: To each object b there is an associated object P b and an arrow e_b : b × P b -> Ω such that for every arrow f : b × a -> Ω there is a unique arrow g : a -> P b making the evident diagram commute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Set, P b is the power set of b and e_b(x,S) = 1 iff x ∈ S. Power objects represent object-of-subobjects categorically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-pointedness (property of a topos)
rubrics_metrics.description: A topos is well-pointed if whenever two arrows f,g : a -> b differ (f ≠ g) then there exists a point p : 1 -> a such that f p ≠ g p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intuitively: functions that differ must differ at some 'point' or element; this property distinguishes Set among toposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Axiom of Choice (AC) in a topos
rubrics_metrics.description: The axiom of choice requires that every surjection f : a -> b has a right inverse s : b -> a (f ∘ s = id_b), i.e., every epimorphic map admits a section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This categorical formulation picks a point of a fiber over each point of b (a global choice function) and is one of the properties that, together with well-pointedness and an NNO, describe Set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural Numbers Object (NNO)
rubrics_metrics.description: An NNO is an object N with a point 0 : 1 -> N and a successor s : N -> N such that for any object b and arrows h : 1 -> b and k : b -> b there is a unique arrow f : N -> b with f ∘ 0 = h and f ∘ s = k ∘ f (recursion/induction property).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formalizes the ability to define functions on N by recursion; together with well-pointedness and AC it helps characterize the category of sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of Set as a topos with extra properties
rubrics_metrics.description: The category of sets can be described as an elementary topos that is (a) well-pointed, (b) has the axiom of choice (AC), and (c) has a natural-numbers object (NNO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three additional properties, when combined with the topos axioms, recover essential features of the usual category of sets; the axioms are weakly consistent with bounded Zermelo set theory per Lawvere.
